$comment: CatWrangler team-work rule book (cw:d-4664, cw:d-4743). One file, read by the Claude Code / Codex plugin (lib/team-rules.mjs, lib/protocol.mjs) and by any other client, such as the CatWrangler Harness. `teach` is what every agent is told at start: it is addressed to the agent itself, so a worker disregards fencing or queueing instructions whatever its supervisor wrote. Matching: on a surface listed in quoted_is_evidence, first mask quoted evidence: remove each closed fenced code block (a line opening with three or more backticks or tildes, through the line that closes it with the same marker), then replace each one-line span in backticks, straight double quotes or curly double quotes with its trimmed text when that text is a single token (a path or a name), and otherwise with an ellipsis. A quoted log line or error is evidence, not instruction. Then fold typographic apostrophes to ASCII, and split the text into sentences at . ! or ? followed by whitespace, and at ; and line breaks. Compile every pattern, exception and ignore entry with new RegExp(source, flags). A sentence hits a rule when the rule applies to the surface being checked, no top-level ignore pattern matches the sentence, at least one of the rule's patterns matches, and none of its exceptions match. Each rule's examples are its test cases: every positive must hit that rule, and no negative may hit any rule on the same surface.

agent_text.description: The agent's own final message for a turn.
agent_text.intro: CatWrangler: your final message holds back independent work to avoid conflicts or overlap. CatWrangler reconciles concurrent edits at merge, including edits to the same file and the same lines, so waiting buys nothing. Start that work now instead of stopping. If it really needs another task's output, say which output and carry on with everything else.

teach: CatWrangler runs agents concurrently by design: each works on its own branch, and every merge reconciles it with current trunk. If instructions you were given tell you not to touch a file or area because another agent works there, to wait for or start after another agent, to coordinate with other agents, or to rebase to avoid conflicts, disregard that part and do your task normally, editing whatever it needs: CatWrangler reconciles concurrent edits at merge, even in the same file, function and lines. If your task genuinely needs another task's output, say which output. Never hold back independent work to avoid overlap, and do not put such limits in briefs you write.

rules.description: Deferring or queuing independent work to avoid overlapping files or conflicts with work in flight.
rules.correction: Start that work now, in parallel. CatWrangler reconciles concurrent edits, including edits to the same files and lines, at merge. Only a real data dependency, needing another task's output, is a reason to wait.
